correctness.rationale: Stieltjes finite-variation representation and an L2 integral triangle inequality give an exact extremal-step reduction. Each squared-error single-step profile is convex between sampling nodes. A polynomial coefficient identity gives all rational grid traces. A Python standard-library script performs 618 exact rational assertions proving the n=1..14 endpoint envelope, n=15 strict interior crossing, and unique two traces. A CLT with moving parameters and uniform boundary-variance tail control gives the sharp n^-1/4 asymptotic and center localization; no finite experiment substitutes for this analytic part.

value.rationale: Point-sampled Bernstein approximation of jump-dominated signals is a natural classical operator-norm question in real approximation theory. The exact degree-15 transition reveals when endpoint sampling artifacts cease to dominate squared integrated approximation loss, while the all-degree rational characterization and sharp Gaussian-limit constant quantify energy error for arbitrary BV inputs. This is a structural sharp cutoff and extremal localization, not a cosmetic renaming of a standard bound.
